Most trees were measured in two "Old Growth"  stands hereby labelled North or South.

Part of the Montezuma NWF, Howland's Island is a multi-use public property. The land area is broken up by several large ponds, swamps, meadows, fields and cattail marshes.  Most of the forested land contains even-aged hardwood stands, though a few very large and old specimens can be found.
Trees on this section of the preserve are subject to annual flooding lasting for a day and up to two weeks.
